question: In September 2021, Adif, the largest beneficiary of NextGenerationEU funds in Spain, awarded Thales a contract worth EUR 93 million to overhaul the signalling and safety systems of the high-speed rail line linking Madrid and Seville, including replacement of the LZB protection system. The work was to be completed by January 2026.

Five years after the contract was awarded, and 10 months after the end of the implementation period, the LZB system is still being used. The Spanish Government used this contract to justify to the Commission its fulfilment of milestone 87 of its recovery and resilience plan, needed to unlock further NextGenerationEU payments.

In other words, to maintain its stream of EU funding, it leveraged an incomplete measure as a guarantee: the LZB system is still active. The repercussions are all too clear: the Urda tragedy – the second fatal railway accident in 2026 – has left 69 people dead. 1.
Will the Commission verify the extent to which the contract awarded by Adif has actually been implemented?
What guarantees does it have that the EU funds paid out have in fact been used for the investments for which they were earmarked?
Will it verify whether the milestones declared by the Spanish Government have been achieved?
